backup.exports_users_roles_api_tokens: Exports users, roles, API tokens, webhooks, registry credentials, GitOps stacks, stack compose history, saved templates and SSO settings as a single JSON file. Audit log and metrics history are intentionally left out - this is a configuration snapshot, not a full database dump.
backup.merged_user_s_and_api: Merged %v user(s) and %v API token(s), plus webhooks/registries/GitOps stacks/stack history/templates/SSO config from the uploaded file. Existing records not present in the file were left untouched.
backup.merges_the_uploaded_file_into: Merges the uploaded file into the current store: records are created or overwritten by ID, nothing already present is deleted. Encrypted fields (registry passwords, GitOps access tokens, stack deploy variables, the SSO client secret, two-factor secrets) only decrypt successfully if this instance uses the same --cluster-secret the backup was taken with.
backup.restore_users_and_settings_from: Restore users and settings from this backup file? Existing records with the same ID will be overwritten.
backup.some_encrypted_fields_could_not: Some encrypted fields could not be decrypted:
backup.this_happens_when_the_backup: This happens when the backup was taken on an admin instance with a different --cluster-secret. The records were still restored - just re-enter the affected password/secret by hand.

events.task_state_transitions_observed_b: Task state transitions observed by the background poller (every 10s) - durable history beyond the live rollout view on a service's page.

file_object.created_this_version_to_repl: Created this version to replace %v.

gitops.deploy_a_stack_straight_from: Deploy a stack straight from a git repo instead of pasting compose YAML by hand. "Sync now" or a poll interval re-fetches the compose file and re-applies it whenever the commit at the configured ref changes.
gitops.remove_gitops_config_for_this: Remove GitOps config for %v? This does not delete the deployed services.
image_updates.tag_isnt_a_version_number: Tag %v isn't a version number - use "Update to latest" to re-pull it.
login.sign_in_to_manage_your: Sign in to manage your cluster
login.too_many_failed_attempts_try: too many failed attempts - try again in %dm
login_2fa.lost_your_phone_enter_one: Lost your phone? Enter one of your recovery codes instead.
node_detail.no_tasks_scheduled_on_this: No tasks scheduled on this node.
node_detail.used_for_placement_constrain: Used for placement constraints (node.labels.zone==a) and spread preferences.
nodes.drain_its_tasks_will_be: Drain %v? Its tasks will be rescheduled elsewhere.
registries.save_without_checking_admin_c: Save without checking (admin can't reach this registry, but the nodes can)
registries.used_automatically_whenever_a: Used automatically whenever an image from one of these registries is pulled - creating or updating a service, deploying a stack, deploy webhooks - and to look up newer tags for image updates, so private images can be updated automatically too. The login is checked against the registry when you save it. Passwords are encrypted at rest (keyed off the cluster secret) and never shown again after saving.
secret_detail.create_a_new_secret_and: Create a new secret and restart the services using %v?
secret_detail.swarm_secrets_are_immutabl: Swarm secrets are immutable, so rotating creates a new secret with the new value and switches every service above to it, keeping the path it's mounted at - their tasks restart with the new value. The current value can't be shown: Docker never returns a secret's value.
secrets.delete_secret_services_still_usi: Delete secret %v? Services still using it will fail to (re)start.
secrets.docker_secrets_are_write_only: Docker secrets are write-only - once created, the value can never be read back through the API (by swarmdash or anyone else).
service_detail.allow_this_hook_to_switch: Allow this hook to switch to a different image repository, not just a different tag
service_detail.no_usage_data_yet_its: No usage data yet - it's collected from every node's agent about once a minute, for running tasks only.
service_detail.post_to_this_url_optional: POST to this URL (optionally with a JSON body {"image":"repo/name:tag"}) to trigger a redeploy from CI - no session or API token needed, the URL itself is the credential. By default an image override may only change the tag/digest of the service's current repository; a hook created with "allow full image override" may switch to any repository.
service_detail.re_pull_the_latest_image: Re-pull the latest image for this tag and redeploy?
service_detail.roll_back_to_the_previous: Roll back to the previous version?
service_detail.webhook_created_copy_it_n: Webhook created - copy it now, it won't be shown again:
service_logs.merged_output_from_every_ta: Merged output from every task/replica of this service.
service_new.with_a_stack_the_service: With a stack, the service is created as <stack>_<name> and shows up under that stack. If the stack is deployed from a compose file, the service isn't in that file - a later deploy with "Remove services not in the file" would remove it.
settings_general.dashboard_shows_a_banne: The dashboard shows a banner when a newer swarmdash release is available. Checking it has your browser ask api.github.com for the latest release directly - the admin server itself never talks to GitHub. Turning this off stops that request entirely, not just the banner.
settings_general.make_every_local_passwo: Make every local-password account set up an authenticator app before it can use swarmdash. SSO accounts and API tokens are not affected. Admins can reset a user's two-factor from Settings → Users.
settings_general.once_an_hour_move_every: Once an hour, move every service whose image has a version tag (1.27.1, v2.3, 8.0.1-jdk17) to the newest tag of the same form in its registry. Patch stays within the current minor version (1.27.1 → 1.27.4), minor within the current major version (1.27.1 → 1.29.0), major takes any newer version (1.27.1 → 2.0.1). Tags like latest are never touched. A service can override this on its page or with the swarmdash.autoupdate label (off, patch, minor, major) under deploy.labels in compose. Each update is recorded in the audit log and sent to webhooks as service_image_updated.
settings_general.require_two_factor_auth: Require two-factor authentication for local accounts
sso.generic_oidc_openid_connect_works: Generic OIDC (OpenID Connect) - works with Okta, Authentik, Keycloak, Google Workspace, Azure AD, Auth0 and any other provider that exposes an issuer discovery document. Local username/password login stays available alongside SSO unless you turn on "Require SSO" below.
sso.local_password_login_is_currently: Local password login is currently disabled - only "Sign in with %v" works on the login page, and POST /login rejects password attempts server-side too. If the identity provider becomes unreachable or misconfigured, every account is locked out until this is switched back off directly in the sso_config table/collection of the admin database (SQLite or MongoDB, whichever this instance is configured to use).
sso.no_accounts_must_be_pre: No - accounts must be pre-created (Settings → Users)
sso.off_by_default_confirm_sso: Off by default. Confirm SSO sign-in actually works end-to-end before turning this on - once enabled, the only way back in without direct database access is the identity provider itself.
sso.optional_comma_separated_leave_blank: (optional, comma-separated - leave blank to allow any)
sso.optional_set_this_if_admin: (optional - set this if admin sits behind a proxy/load balancer; otherwise derived from the request)
sso.redirect_uri_to_register_with: Redirect URI to register with your identity provider:
sso.require_sso_disable_local_username: Require SSO - disable local username/password login
sso.swarmdash_fetches_issuer_well_known: swarmdash fetches <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration to find the provider's authorization/token/userinfo endpoints.
sso.turns_sign_in_off_without: Turns sign-in off without discarding the saved configuration (issuer, client ID/secret) so it can be re-enabled later.
stack_deploy.key_value_per_line_like: (KEY=value per line, like a .env file - stored encrypted with the stack's history)
stack_deploy.remove_services_not_in_the: Remove services not in the file (the stack's other services are deleted; their volumes are kept)
stack_deploy.saves_the_compose_file_abov: Saves the compose file above (not its variables) to Stacks → Templates. Saving under an existing template's name replaces it.
stack_deploy.supports_the_compose_featur: Supports the compose features that map onto swarm services: image, entrypoint/command, environment, labels, user/working_dir/hostname, healthcheck, logging, ulimits/sysctls/capabilities, ports and volumes (short and long syntax), networks with aliases, secrets/configs with target/uid/gid/mode, and deploy.* (replicas/mode, placement, resources, update/rollback config, restart policy, endpoint_mode). Top-level volumes may set a driver and driver_opts (e.g. NFS); top-level configs may carry inline content:. Secrets must already exist (Secrets page) and are referenced with external: true. ${VAR} references are filled from Variables below. Anything else is reported in the preview and ignored.
stack_deploy.this_stack_is_managed_by: This stack is managed by GitOps (%v) - a manual deploy is overwritten by the next sync that finds a new commit. Change the file in git instead.
stack_detail.deployed_by_gitops_from_edi: Deployed by GitOps from %v (%v:%v) - edit the file in git; a manual edit here is overwritten by the next sync that finds a new commit.
stack_detail.no_compose_file_stored_for: No compose file stored for this stack yet - it was deployed before swarmdash kept stack history, or outside swarmdash. "Edit" starts from a compose file generated from its running services; the first deploy from there starts the history.
stack_detail.redeploy_v_of_services_that: Redeploy v%v of %v? Services that version doesn't define are removed (their volumes are kept).
stack_logs.merged_output_from_every_serv: Merged output from every service of this stack, ordered by time (UTC).
swarm.also_remove_unused_volumes_data: Also remove unused volumes (data loss risk)
swarm.autolock_managers_encrypt_tls_keys: Autolock managers (encrypt TLS keys/raft data at rest)
swarm.clean_up_unused_containers_images: Clean up unused containers, images and networks on every node in the cluster?
swarm.configuration_that_applies_cluster: Configuration that applies cluster-wide, as set in the swarm spec. Raft and dispatcher timing are set at init and rarely need changing - wrong values here can affect cluster stability.
swarm.could_not_be_removed_check: %v could not be removed - check the audit log.
swarm.default_task_log_driver_blank: Default task log driver (blank = engine default)
swarm.deletes_the_leftover_container_beh: Deletes the leftover container behind every task in failed or rejected state, across all nodes. Running tasks and their history for successful deploys are untouched.
swarm.force_restart_all_replicated_servi: Force-restart all %v replicated services so Swarm re-places their tasks across every current node?
swarm.force_the_swarm_to_generate: Force the swarm to generate a new root CA certificate? All node certificates will be reissued as they renew.
swarm.generates_a_new_cluster_root: Generates a new cluster root certificate; all node certificates are reissued as they're renewed. External CAs configured:
swarm.manager_autolock_is_now_on: Manager autolock is now on - save this unlock key, it won't be shown again:
swarm.nodes_could_not_be_reached: %v node could not be reached.|%v nodes could not be reached.
swarm.reduce_load_left_over_from: Reduce load left over from normal cluster operation: dead task containers that outlived their usefulness, and images/networks/volumes/containers nothing references anymore.
swarm.remove_all_unused_images_not: Remove all unused images, not just dangling ones
swarm.remove_the_container_behind_every: Remove the container behind every failed/rejected task across the cluster?
swarm.removed_failed_task_containers: Removed %v failed task container.|Removed %v failed task containers.
swarm.replicated_services_will_be_force: %v replicated service will be force-restarted|%v replicated services will be force-restarted
swarm.root_ca_rotation_started_new: Root CA rotation started. New node certificates will roll out as they're renewed.
swarm.rotate_the_manager_join_token: Rotate the manager join token? Existing tokens will stop working.
swarm.rotate_the_worker_join_token: Rotate the worker join token? Existing tokens will stop working.
swarm.run_on_the_node_you: Run on the node you want to add:
swarm.runs_a_docker_system_prune: Runs a docker system prune equivalent on every node: stopped containers, unused networks, and dangling images. Nothing that's running or in use is touched.
swarm.swarm_only_weighs_current_node: Swarm only weighs current node load when placing new tasks - it never moves an already-running task onto a node that joined later. After adding or removing nodes, force-restart every replicated service so the scheduler re-places all their tasks across the nodes currently in the cluster (%v). Each service still rolls per its own update policy (parallelism/delay/order), so this doesn't take everything down at once. Global-mode services aren't included - they already run one task per eligible node automatically.
swarm.task_history_retention_limit_blank: Task history retention limit (blank = engine default, negative = keep forever)
swarm.these_three_are_fixed_at: These three are fixed at docker swarm init time and can't be changed afterward.
templates_gallery.compose_templates_for_: Compose templates for common self-hosted services, plus your own (saved with "Save as template" on the deploy form). "Use template" pre-fills the deploy form - review and edit (especially placeholder passwords) before deploying.
tokens.for_ci_cd_or_scripts: For CI/CD or scripts: pass Authorization: Bearer <token> to call any swarmdash endpoint without a browser session. Scoped the same way as user accounts - admin tokens are full-access, viewer tokens are read-only. Tokens created before roles existed have no stored role and are treated as admin.
tokens.token_created_copy_it_now: Token created - copy it now, it won't be shown again:
topology.no_services_are_attached_to: No services are attached to an overlay network yet.
topology.services_connected_by_a_shared: Services connected by a shared overlay network. Drag nodes to rearrange, scroll to zoom, click a node to trace its connections.
topology.these_services_dont_share_an: These services don't share an overlay network with anything else, so they don't appear on the map above.
users.admins_have_full_access_viewers: Admins have full access. Viewers are read-only: no create/update/delete actions, no console access, and Settings pages are hidden.
users.reset_two_factor_for_theyll: Reset two-factor for %v? They'll sign in with just their password until they set it up again.
users.sso_account_no_local_password: SSO account (no local password - see Settings → SSO)
volume_backups.backups_run_in_the_backgr: Backups run in the background on the node that holds the volume and are stored there, in the agent's backup directory. To move a volume to another node, download its backup and upload it on the other node.
volume_backups.for_a_consistent_copy_of: For a consistent copy of a database, scale its service to 0 first - files are read while the volume stays in use.
volume_backups.no_backups_on_this_node: No backups on this node yet.
volume_backups.restore_history_is_kept_u: Restore history is kept until the node's agent restarts.
volume_backups.restore_this_backup_into_: Restore this backup into volume %s? Files in the backup overwrite files with the same name.
volume_backups.tar_gz_of_the_volumes: A .tar.gz of the volume's contents - one downloaded from here, or made with tar -czf backup.tar.gz -C /path/to/data .
volume_backups.volume_backups_are_turned: Volume backups are turned off on this node: its agent was started without a backup directory. Start it with --backup-dir (or SWARMDASH_BACKUP_DIR) pointing at a mounted host directory.
volumes.delete_volume_data_will_be: Delete volume %v? Data will be lost.
webhooks.posted_a_json_body_event: POSTed a JSON body {event, target, message, time} when a service stays below its desired replica count for more than 2 minutes (and when it recovers), or when a node goes down/comes back.
